newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean biggest union group cancels Monday strike.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean biggest union group cancels Monday strike.

text.p: South Korea's biggest union group announced it was calling off a one-hour strike on Monday and reconsidering plans for a three-hour strike on Thursday.

"Our primary purpose was to block revision (of the labour law) by the close of the parliamentary session, and now we see it's impossible for the revision to be made within the session we are cancelling Monday's strike," said Chung Young-sook, a senior official of the Federation of Korea Trade Unions.
The current parliamentary session is scheduled to end on Wednesday and the labour reform bill has not yet been presented to parliament for full debate.
"We are reconsidering Thursday's plan and will decide later whether or not to hold the strike," she said.
The federation had threatened to call one-hour walkouts by its 1.2 million members across the country from 1.00 p.m. (0400 GMT) on Monday.
Last Friday the country's second biggest union group, the Korea Confederation of Trade Unions, postponed a four-hour strike on the reform issue.

Opposition parties have called for a delay in pushing through a new labour bill that allows layoffs and flexible work hours. The ruling New Korea Party wants to adopt the bill during the current session of parliament.
